item.title: IASTM for Calf
clinicalUse: Calf stiffness/myofascial discomfort as adjunct before mobility/loading
patientPosition: Prone or supine with calf supported.
contact: Instrument over gastrocnemius/soleus; avoid popliteal fossa and varicosities.
item.visualCue: Instrument along calf → short controlled dose → dorsiflexion/calf raise re-test.

subTechniques.name: Gastrocnemius–soleus — IASTM
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, long sitting, prone or weight-bearing depending on the technique.
subTechniques.contact: Appropriate instrument edge over intact skin at Gastrocnemius–soleus with conservative pressure.
subTechniques.direction: Use light-to-moderate scanning/treatment strokes; bruising is not the goal.
subTechniques.dosage: Often 30–120 seconds per small area followed by active movement/loading.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
